metadata.title: AI Use Cases | Sébastien Donné | TKoidra
metadata.description: Functional AI demonstrators, live and testable — from framing to production, illustrated by use cases in insurance, real estate, and compliance.

appLink.label: Open the application
appLink.coldStartNote: ⏳ **First load: about 1 minute.** To keep costs down, the demo goes to sleep when no one is using it. On first access, the server restarts: the page may stay blank in the meantime, which is normal. After that, it responds normally.

assurconseil.title: AssurConseil RAG
assurconseil.description: Agentic RAG assistant for insurance contract interpretation, with a Claude / Mistral comparison in document mode.
assurconseil.demonstrates: Industrialising a RAG: evaluation before production, cost guardrails, proven European inference, progressive deployment.
assurconseil.challenge: Insurance advisors must navigate dozens of pages of general terms to answer client questions accurately, under regulatory duty-to-advise obligations — a misread clause or wrongly cited guarantee exposes the insurer to liability.
assurconseil.solution: An agentic RAG assistant that routes each question to the most suitable pattern (ReAct for direct lookups, Plan-and-Execute for multi-part questions), with mandatory source citation and explicit refusal to answer when no supporting document exists — a demo built on fictional contracts and a fictional company (ARESIA Assurances), illustrating an agentic architecture for regulated advisory use cases. In document mode, the same question is sent in parallel to Claude and Mistral Large 3 (Mistral inference run in the EU): answers side by side, with latency, tokens and cost.

features.title: Adaptive ReAct / Plan-and-Execute Routing
features.description: A router detects question complexity and switches between direct retrieval (ReAct) and sub-question decomposition (Plan-and-Execute).

features.title: Anti-Hallucination Guardrail
features.description: Mandatory citation of source articles; an explicit "not found" response rather than a fabricated answer when information is absent from the documents.

features.title: Full Reasoning Traceability
features.description: Every graph step (router, retrieve, evaluate, synthesize) is logged in an inspectable trace_log, from question to final answer.

features.title: Your Contract, Two Engines
features.description: Upload a contract: temporary in-memory index, separate from the corpus. The same question goes in parallel to Claude and Mistral Large 3 (EU inference); answers side by side with latency, tokens and estimated cost.

image.alt: Screenshot of the Claude / Mistral Large 3 comparison on AssurConseil RAG: an answer to a question about a provident contract's deductibles, with cited sources, latency, tokens and cost shown for each engine.

fraud.title: Fraud Agent
fraud.description: Pre-assessment agent for P&C insurance claims: business rules set the routing, a Claude agent proposes, a claims handler decides.
fraud.demonstrates: Designing a bounded agent for a regulated business: what the code decides, what the agent proposes, what the human approves, with measured cost and latency.
fraud.tag: Agentic AI · Human in the Loop
fraud.challenge: In a claims department, most cases are simple, but those that call for an investigation or a recovery claim against a liable third party require cross-checking several documents. Handing this work to AI raises three questions: who decides the routing, what happens when the model gets it wrong, and what does it cost?
fraud.solution: On fictional claims, business rules compute a score out of 50 and set the routing (straight-through processing, investigation, fraud-unit alert). The agent cannot change it. A Claude agent is called only when useful, when the case is suspicious or a police report is provided. It picks its tools, returns a structured proposal, then stops: a claims handler approves or rejects it with a reason, before the agent drafts a letter that is never actually sent. Thresholds are demonstration choices, not calibrated on real data.

features.title: Rules first, AI when useful
features.description: Score and routing come from deterministic rules. A clean case without a police report triggers no AI call.

features.title: An agent that picks its tools
features.description: Depending on the case, the agent checks the repair shop's history or computes the recovery amount. Every step shows in a log (tool, input, output, duration), and amounts are recomputed by the code.

features.title: Mandatory human approval
features.description: The handler approves, or rejects with a reason. A recovery letter draft and a D+5 / D+15 / D+30 plan follow, marked "never actually sent".

metrics: 15 live analyses per day, then a labelled replay (measured on 01/10/2026)

image.alt: Screenshot of an analysis on Fraud Agent: rules score of 0 out of 50, straight-through routing, the agent's step-by-step run and the start of its proposal, on a fictional claim.

methodBridge.label: Same method as AssurConseil RAG: cut the risks before adding features, measure before announcing a figure, rehearse in preview before going to production.

agap.title: AGAP
agap.description: AI-arbitrated project portfolio prioritization, free of Business/IT bias.
agap.demonstrates: Tooling a portfolio decision: surfacing Business/IT gaps and arbitrating through scenarios, with tracked justifications.
agap.challenge: A Portfolio Director arbitrates dozens of projects every year based on structurally biased Business and IT declarations: Business overstates business impact, IT overstates effort and technical risk to protect itself. Without a mediation mechanism, final arbitration becomes a political power struggle rather than an objective decision.
agap.solution: A governance application that has a Claude agent separately challenge each Business and IT declaration, computes a confidence index and an adjusted attractiveness score, then visualizes perception conflicts before final arbitration — a demo built on a fictional 6-project portfolio, illustrating neutral AI mediation between two parties with diverging interests.

features.title: Multi-Role AI Challenger
features.description: A Claude agent separately interrogates Business (perceived value) and IT (estimated effort), generates clarifying questions, and computes a confidence index per declaration.

features.title: Conflict Map
features.description: Visual mapping of the Business/IT perception delta, with a conflict threshold configurable at the deployment level (currently 20 points) to flag projects needing mediation before arbitration.

features.title: Scenarios & Arbitration Cut-Line
features.description: Side-by-side project ranking under two scoring scenarios (MVP / Full) with an adjustable cut-line, plus forced inclusion always justified and logged.

image.alt: Screenshot of the AGAP demo dashboard: a portfolio of 6 fictional projects with their arbitration status, in read-only demonstration mode.

lexguard.title: LexGuard
lexguard.description: Detects red-flag signals in contracts before signature.
lexguard.demonstrates: Making a contract readable for a non-lawyer: red-flag signal detection and a plain-language verdict.
lexguard.challenge: The mayor of a rural town, with no legal department, signs a telecom equipment contract under sales pressure — one that conceals a second leasing agreement with a long commitment term and near-impossible termination. Some towns have been sued for tens of thousands of euros after the fact.
lexguard.solution: A demonstration that analyzes a contract submitted as a PDF and flags, before signature, the warning signs of a risky arrangement (concealed contract, abnormal duration, tacit renewal) — in plain language, without ever ruling on the contract's legality or a company's reliability.

features.title: Red-flag signal detection
features.description: Identifies patterns of risky contractual arrangements.

features.title: Plain-language verdict
features.description: 3-level assessment, no legal jargon.

features.title: No application-side storage
features.description: The document is processed in memory and is not stored by the application. The AI provider (Anthropic) retains transmitted data for 30 days, under its default policy.

image.alt: Screenshot of the LexGuard homepage: contract upload, an example of a detected warning signal, and the guarantee that no uploaded document is stored.

comex.title: Comex
comex.description: Strategic framing and alignment through AI.
comex.demonstrates: Structuring AI framing: from questionnaire to two AI-costed implementation paths.
comex.challenge: Executive committees face a growing volume of AI initiatives without structured tooling to prioritize, frame, and align them with company strategic objectives in a controlled timeframe.
comex.solution: An AI proposal generator powered by Claude: a structured framing questionnaire (19 questions), followed by an AI clarification exchange (up to 4 targeted questions), leading to two implementation proposals — a "quick" one (under 3 months, existing stack) and a "balanced" one (3-6 month MVP) — with budget, timeline and risks estimated by the AI.

features.title: Framing + AI Clarification
features.description: 19 structured questions, followed by an AI clarification exchange (up to 4 targeted questions) to refine the diagnosis.

features.title: Two Costed Proposals
features.description: A "quick" proposal (under 3 months, existing stack) and a "balanced" proposal (3-6 month MVP), with budget, timeline and risks estimated by the AI.

features.title: Tailored to Your Environment
features.description: Proposals take the declared IT stack into account (cloud and AI provider already in place).

sirene.title: Sirene
sirene.demonstrates: Making a public API accessible in natural language, with a lightweight model (Claude Haiku).
sirene.challenge: Sales and operations teams waste valuable time identifying and qualifying companies through the standard INSEE Sirene interface. Rigid filter syntax and lack of semantic understanding hinder adoption.
sirene.solution: An AI assistant that understands natural language queries and interrogates the INSEE Sirene API to return structured and filtered results — with no technical knowledge required from the user.

features.title: Natural Language Queries
features.description: Translation of the query into Sirene API parameters by an LLM (Claude Haiku).

features.title: Sector and Region Filters
features.description: NAF sector and region inferred from free-form expressions, with a filter on administrative status (active or discontinued companies).

features.title: Results Export
features.description: CSV and Excel export of results.

dvf.title: DVF
dvf.description: Real estate transaction search and analysis.
dvf.demonstrates: Using open land-registry data: address search and municipality-level price statistics.
dvf.challenge: Analyzing DVF (Property Value Requests) data published by the DGFiP is tedious: multi-GB raw CSV format, no native visualization, and difficulty cross-referencing with geographic data.
dvf.solution: A search platform for real estate and land transactions, with land price statistics by municipality from DGFiP open data.

features.title: Median Land Price by Municipality
features.description: Median price per m² and land area, with year-by-year evolution, calculated for each municipality from DVF transaction data.

features.title: Address-Based Transaction Search
features.description: Geolocated search for real estate and land sale transactions around an address, with automatic fallback to a wider radius.

verifid.title: ID Document Verifier
verifid.description: AI-powered document quality control and MRZ consistency check.
verifid.demonstrates: Combining AI reading with a deterministic calculation (MRZ check digits) to make verification more reliable.
verifid.challenge: A subscription file with an illegible or incomplete ID gets stuck until a handler notices it and contacts the client — a back-and-forth cycle that degrades completion rates and burdens the back office.
verifid.solution: A demonstration that checks the quality of an identity document at upload time (legibility, completeness, framing) and has the AI read its MRZ, then checks its mathematical consistency against ICAO 9303 — without ever judging its authenticity.

features.title: Instant quality control
features.description: Detection in seconds of blurry photos, glare, or partially out-of-frame documents, before a file ever reaches a handler.

features.title: Verifiable MRZ consistency
features.description: Deterministic ICAO 9303 check-digit calculation (ID card and passport), with the details shown. The characters are read by the AI: the calculation is transparent, the reading can be wrong.

features.title: Front/back cross-check
features.description: Comparison of the document number between both sides of the card, as an additional consistency signal.

metadata.title: AI Method: From Diagnosis to Production | TKoidra
metadata.description: A three-stage AI method — diagnose, build, operate — with guardrails, evaluation and compliance from the start, proven online.
metadata.ogTitle: AI Method: From Diagnosis to Production

methode.title: From Diagnosis to Controlled Production
methode.lead: Most generative AI projects don't fail for lack of a model. They fail between prototype and production: data, security, costs, compliance, adoption. My method addresses these issues from day one, in three stages. Each stage is illustrated by what I actually did on my online demonstrators, using fictional data.
methode.stepperLabel: The three phases of the method

phases.name: Diagnose
phases.goal: Decide quickly and well. Where does AI create value, and is the project worth building?
actions: Start from the mission, not the tool: what business problem, for whom, and how will it be measured?
A real inventory: what actually runs, not what the documentation says — data, information system, security, regulatory constraints.
Use cases grounded in the field: confronting management's vision with the reality of the teams.
Prioritisation by value, feasibility and risk, operating cost included.
A go/no-go decision, with success criteria and an acceptance floor set before writing the first line.

proof.text: Before adding a single feature, I audited the demo in production. The live version did not match the documentation, no spending cap was confirmed, and a secondary instance remained public. These findings defined the first batch: guardrails before features.

tools.name: Comex
tools.detail: framing in **19 questions**, two implementation proposals

tools.name: AGAP
tools.detail: arbitration of a project portfolio: Business/IT perception gap, scenarios, cut-off line

practices: An identified executive sponsor, and baseline KPIs measured before the project, to compare before and after.
Precisely qualified needs: usage volume, error tolerance, acceptable latency, confidentiality, need for explainability.
Data quality assessed on its six dimensions: completeness, uniqueness, timeliness, validity, accuracy, consistency.
The simplest solution first: an existing tool, then a well-designed prompt, then document grounding (RAG). Fine-tuning only if necessary.
Regulatory risk qualified early: as soon as a system influences a decision about a person (employment, credit, access to a right), legal advice before developing.
Start with a high-impact, feasible scope, then expand.

phases.name: Build
phases.goal: Deliver a prototype that runs online, measured, safe and compliant. Not a throwaway demo.
actions: Short batches, each testable and deployable, with a read-only analysis and a validated plan before any change.
Guardrails first: spending caps, quotas, input limits, neutral error messages, secrets kept out of the code, least-privilege accounts.
A model chosen on explicit criteria: quality on the use case, cost, latency, output format, provider compliance.
Answers grounded in sources: mandatory citations, explicit refusal when information is missing.
Evaluation before any deployment: reference question set, edge cases, go/no-go floor, measured cost.
Compliance by design: data retention checked in the providers' official policies, accurate consent, limits displayed.

proof.text: I added the Claude / Mistral Large 3 comparison in several sub-batches. Mistral Large 3 was preferred to a more expensive model, for its cost and a comparable response format. Before deployment, the comparison was evaluated on **20 questions**: **40 out of 40 calls** succeeded, the floor was met by both engines, actual cost **$0.39**. Data retention was checked in both providers' policies, and Mistral inference goes through the European endpoint, with evidence in the audit log.

practices: Shared responsibility clarified: whatever the provider, the company remains responsible for its data and its access.
Security across the whole lifecycle: least privilege, audited access, secrets in a vault, minimisation and anonymisation of personal data.
Human in the loop where errors are costly: review before release, final decision by a human.
Model limitations handled by design: hallucinations, bias, edge cases, outdated knowledge.
A continuous integration and deployment pipeline, with automated tests on every change.
Documented choices and limits, for users as well as auditors.

phases.name: Operate
phases.goal: That the solution holds over time, costs what was planned, and is actually used.
actions: Progressive deployment: the new version is deployed without traffic, tested under real conditions, then switched over. Rollback is ready in one command.
Observability: logs without user content, audit lines, cost tracked for every request.
Incident management: root cause established from the logs before any fix.
Planned maintenance: recurring checks, dependencies, regressions, dated log.
Tracking value and adoption: KPIs compared with the baseline, user feedback, adjustments.

proof.text: Upload sessions were cut off after 5 minutes. The logs showed connection closures at **301 seconds**, aligned with the service's maximum timeout. The fix was validated by an **11-minute** test session. Same rigour on performance: after diagnosis (computation precision, number of processors), indexing a document went **from 480 to 142 seconds**.

practices: Service level objectives (SLOs) on the signals that matter: latency, traffic, saturation, errors.
Budget alerts and quotas, so that a cost overrun is detected before the invoice.
Quality monitored over time: re-evaluation after every change of model, prompt or data.
Human review of answers after the fact, to feed continuous improvement.
Tested backups and a recovery plan, not just written ones.
Regulatory and security watch: patches, and changes to the GDPR as well as the AI Act.

threads.title: Six common threads, from the first day to the last

items.title: Proven value
items.text: KPIs defined before, measured after. If the gain isn't there, we adjust or stop.

items.title: Measured quality
items.text: We decide on evaluation results, not on an impression.

items.title: Responsible AI and compliance
items.text: Transparency, confidentiality, fairness, GDPR, AI Act transparency obligations, and a clear answer to the question "who is responsible?".

items.title: Controlled costs
items.text: Caps, quotas, visible cost per request, hidden costs anticipated.

items.title: Sovereignty and reversibility
items.text: Interchangeable providers, a European endpoint when relevant, no forced lock-in.

items.title: Adoption and skills
items.text: A sponsor, the mission restated before the tool, trained teams. It has been my foundation for 15 years, in change management, agile facilitation and Product Ownership.

operatingMode.title: My operating mode: AI accelerates, humans decide

steps.title: Plan and get it approved
steps.text: No change without an approved plan.

steps.title: Deliver in small batches
steps.text: One commit per topic, automated tests, a reviewed preview.

steps.title: Keep control of production
steps.text: Any command that touches it is run by a human, after verification.

operatingMode.quote: I develop with AI coding agents under this protocol. It is what makes it possible to move fast without losing control, and it is the same discipline I bring to your teams.

items.title: A promise of ROI before measurement.
A disguised client deployment.
items.text: My demonstrators use fictional data: they prove the method, not a result at a client.
